tool_calls.name: lookup_refund_policy
tool_calls.arguments: {"query":"How the refund amount is calculated; unit's paid price after discount"}

messages.name: lookup_refund_policy
messages.content: {"ok": true, "sections": [{"citation": "refund-policy/v1/amount", "title": "Refund amount", "text": "The refund for a unit is what was paid for that unit: its price minus its share of any discount. The shares are fixed once, when the order is recorded, and never recalculated: when a paid total is split among identical units, each unit gets the total divided by the number of units, rounded down to the smallest unit of the currency, and what is left over is added one smallest unit at a time to the last units, so no unit is refunded more than its price. Shipping charges are not part of the amount."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v1/remaining", "title": "Each unit is refunded once", "text": "Each unit is refunded at most once, in full. A unit that was already refunded cannot be refunded again. A request for more units than are left is not paid; the assistant can offer the units that remain."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v1/validity", "title": "How long a proposal is valid", "text": "A proposal can be confirmed, approved or paid only strictly before it expires, 72 hours after it is created. After that it expires together with its confirmation and approval, and a new proposal is needed. A proposal also stops being valid if the order or this policy changes before it is paid. Expiry stops new payments only: a refund already paid stays paid, and its receipt can always be retrieved."}], "note": "Cite a section by its citation ID, exactly as given."}

messages.text: The refund was R$49.00 because that was the amount paid for the box after its share of any discount; refunds are based on the amount paid for the unit, not its listed price. Shipping is also excluded from refunds. (refund-policy/v1/amount)
That makes sense. The R$49.00 refund is what I want.
